name: FDA approves gene therapy for young children
summary: The US FDA approved Casgevy on 1 July 2026 for children aged 2 and older with sickle cell disease, which it calls the first gene therapy for this age group.
keyPoints: The US FDA approved Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) for patients aged 2 years and older on 1 July 2026.
It covers sickle cell disease with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises and transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia.
The FDA first approved Casgevy and Lyfgenia for sickle cell disease in December 2023, for patients aged 12 and older.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 1 July 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) for patients aged 2 years and older.

The FDA says it is the first gene therapy approved for patients aged 2 years and older with sickle cell disease.

The approval covers sickle cell disease with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises, and transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The FDA first approved Casgevy and Lyfgenia for sickle cell disease in December 2023, for patients aged 12 and older.

The FDA notes that Casgevy is the first FDA-approved therapy that uses CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing.

Before the Casgevy infusion, patients receive a high-intensity preparatory treatment called myeloablative conditioning.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.
